title: budgeted-regression-guardrails-heuristic-templates
content:
Context:
This is a working draft of a lightweight, budget-driven guardrail system for deploying lower-cost model/quantization variants while bounding quality regressions. The goal: make it easy for product and infra teams to evaluate cheap variants with a small, well-defined eval budget and automatic gating logic that ties into rollouts/fallbacks.

Problem we solve:
- Teams want to reduce per-token unit cost by switching traffic to cheaper configs (quantized weights, smaller models, lower token limits, batching tweaks).
- Each cheap variant has a non-zero risk of downstream quality regressions that are costly in product metrics (e.g., CTR, NPS, conversion) or safety.
- Running full eval suites for every variant is expensive. We need a pragmatic, budgeted gating approach that:
  - limits eval cost (monetary + compute)
  - provides an interpretable pass/fail decision tied to expected business impact
  - supports staged rollouts and automatic rollback/fallbacks

High-level proposal (heuristic templates):
1) Micro-eval budget envelope (per experiment):
   - Default budget: $300 (configurable per customer/route). Rationale: allows ~3–10k human-labeled prompts for micro-evals or ~30–100k automated synthetic checks depending on method.
   - Budget components: labeling cost, annotation QA overhead, compute for eval runs, annotation tooling.

2) Multi-signal gate (three layers, fast -> slow):
   - Layer A (fast proxies, automated): smoke checks that run on live traffic samples or synthetic sets. Metrics: perplexity shift, token-level edit distance heuristic, answer-compat ratio. Budget impact: low. Fail -> immediate block.
   - Layer B (automated evals on held-out testbeds): run 2–10k examples through both baseline and variant to compute delta on key eval metrics (EM/ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim). Budget impact: medium. Uses server compute.
   - Layer C (targeted human review): a small human-eval sample focused on degradation-sensitive intents (n=300–1,000). Compute expected business loss estimate. Budget impact: high per-sample, but small N.

3) Decision rules (example heuristics):
   - Define baseline Q metric (Q_baseline) and variant Q (Q_variant) on the chosen eval metric(s).
   - Delta = Q_variant - Q_baseline (positive is better).
   - Pass if BOTH: 
       a) Delta_quality >= -0.5 percentage points (absolute) on primary metric OR estimated revenue-risk <= $X per 100k queries; AND
       b) Layer A pass (no catastrophic heuristics); AND
       c) Human-sampled error severity mean <= 1.5 on 1–5 rubric (if Layer C run).
   - If fail, recommend: keep traffic on baseline OR fallback to a safer variant (e.g., higher precision quant) and re-run tests.

Sample spreadsheet columns (sheet: linked above). These should be present in our canonical eval-cost model sheet to make gating calculations auditable and reproducible: (each column name as a header)
   - config_name
   - variant_description (e.g., 8-bit-quant-static, int4-llm-fp16kv)
   - baseline_name
   - avg_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd (numeric)
   - estimated_monthly_tokens (numeric)
   - baseline_quality_score (percent)
   - variant_quality_score (percent)
   - delta_quality_points (variant - baseline)
   - micro_eval_samples (N)
   - micro_eval_cost_usd
   - human_eval_samples (N)
   - human_eval_cost_usd
   - expected_savings_usd_per_100k_tokens (formula)
   - expected_monthly_savings_usd (formula)
   - estimated_revenue_risk_usd_per_100k (formula)
   - net_expected_value_usd_per_100k (formula: savings - risk)

Example formulas (Google Sheets syntax, plain text):
   - expected_savings_usd_per_100k = (baseline_cost_per_1k - variant_cost_per_1k)
   - expected_monthly_savings_usd = expected_savings_usd_per_100k * (estimated_monthly_tokens / 100000)
   - estimated_revenue_risk_usd_per_100k = sensitivity_coefficient * (-delta_quality_points) * baseline_revenue_per_100k
     * sensitivity_coefficient is derived from product-level regressions (0.1–0.5 typical).

Worked example (rounded):
   - baseline_cost_per_1k = $1.20, variant_cost_per_1k = $0.72 -> savings = $0.48 per 1k
   - estimated_monthly_tokens = 50,000,000 -> monthly_savings = 0.48 * (50,000,000 / 1,000) = $24,000
   - measured delta_quality_points = -0.4pp on primary metric
   - baseline_revenue_per_100k = $1,200 (estimated downstream revenue per 100k requests)
   - sensitivity_coefficient = 0.2 -> estimated_risk = 0.2 * 0.4 * 1,200 = $96 per 100k -> monthly_risk ~ $48k scaled (note: double-check scaling units in sheet)
   - net_expected_value would then compare $24k savings vs risk; if risk > savings, gate fails.

Notes on sensitivity_coefficient calibration:
   - This is product-specific. For chat-UI product, we observed (conservatively) 0.15–0.25 impact factor from small quality drops on conversion funnels. For internal infra metrics it can be lower (0.02–0.08). Add per-route coefficients in the sheet.

Automation + rollouts integration:
- gating service should be able to call the spreadsheet API or a compact JSON model that contains thresholds per route.
- On-pass: enable canary at 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with health checks at each step (latency, error rate, quality probe failure rate).
- On-fail at any stage: automatic traffic re-route to baseline and Jira ticket creation with eval snapshot attached.

Runbook (short):
- Step 0: Owner files an experiment row in the canonical sheet (link above) with estimated traffic and budget.
- Step 1: Run Layer A smoke checks on 1k live-sampled requests (automated).
- Step 2: If A passes, schedule Layer B: run 5k offline evals comparing baseline vs variant.
- Step 3: If B passes, run Layer C on n=300 targeted human samples (prioritize high-risk intents).
- Step 4: Compute net_expected_value and apply decision rules.
- Step 5: If pass, kick-off canary rollout per rollout policy. Attach eval artifacts to JIRA-OPT-4372.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Decide default micro-eval budget per tenant and whether to offer adjustable tiers (low/medium/high).
- [ ] Agree on a small set of primary metrics to use as canonical for each product route (chat, search, summarization). Link: CONFLUENCE-OPT/quality-metrics-mapping.
- [ ] Define a standard human-eval rubric (1–5 severity) and sampling strategy for Layer C. (Owner: Evan)
- [ ] Add automation to compute sensitivity_coefficient from historical A/B regressions; currently a manual cell in sheet. (Owner: Lina)
- [ ] Instrument rollout service to automatically attach micro-eval results and create a rollback JIRA if pass->fail during canary. (Owner: Samir)

Quick checklist for an experiment owner (copy into PR notes):
- [ ] Add experiment row to canonical sheet with baseline and variant costs + traffic estimate.
- [ ] Confirm micro-eval budget and fund code path for human evals (if needed).
- [ ] Run Layer A smoke, record artifacts (logs, diffs).
- [ ] Upload Layer B outputs (CSV of paired scores) to the artifact store.
- [ ] Kick off Layer C annotation batch (if required).
- [ ] Approve or reject via decision rules, record rationale in JIRA.

Appendix: short heuristics cheat-sheet (for engineers):
- If delta_quality_points >= -0.2pp and expected_savings_per_100k > $100 -> auto-allow micro-canary (1%).
- If delta_quality_points between -0.2pp and -1.0pp -> require Layer C human eval and compute full net_expected_value.
- If delta_quality_points <= -1.0pp -> block (fail) unless revenue-risk calibration shows savings >> risk (rare).
- If Layer A flags any safety keywords or hallucination heuristics -> immediate block, escalate to safety team.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and conservative in thresholds to avoid shipping bad regressions. We expect iteration after ~10 experiments to calibrate the sensitivity coefficients and default budgets. Please comment inline or add suggestions to JIRA-OPT-4372.

Recent related artifacts (examples):
- small-batch-int4-eval-results-2026-01.csv (attached in artifact store)
- sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcD_example_sheet_id (canonical cost/eval model)

End of draft.
